paper.title_en: Shadows and Polarimetric Signatures of Rotating Simpson-Visser Black Holes with Thick Disk Illumination
paper.abstract_en: In this manuscript, we investigate the shadow and polarization images of a Simpson-Visser rotating black hole surrounded by a ballistic approximation accretion flow model. Solving the numerically geodesic and radiative transfer equations, we discuss the influence of the regularization parameter $g$, spin parameter $a$, and observer inclination angle $θ_o$ on the resulting images at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$ with an infalling motion. The results interpret that, a bright circular ring corresponding to higher-order images is observed, accompanied by an inner region of decreased intensity. Both $g$ and $a$ has little influence on the size of the higher-order images, but significantly changes their shape and intensity distribution. Whereas, variation in $θ_o$ modify the image morphology, producing a crescent-shaped bright region on the left side. Finally, the polarization patterns trace the brightness distribution and vary with both $g$ and $a$, reflecting the spacetime structure. These results demonstrates that the intensity and polarization in thick disk models provide probes of Simpson-Visser rotating black holes and near-horizon accretion physics.
